main_concern: The strongest completion signal is a manual prune receipt and a self-check with --skip-carrier-probe, which may validate code paths without proving the integrated run-time behavior. This creates narrative self-consistency that hides the missing end-to-end execution evidence.
top_risks: E2E cache governance is claimed as integrated, but the only observed deletion event is a manually invoked prune command; the automatic after-run retention path may still be untested in vivo.

The public/private boundary check passing is reported at the scan level; without seeing which markers were removed or whether semantic/path references to ~/.cap/identity.md remain, residual leakage risk is unquantified.

Exit criteria in the open-loop queue may be stated in negotiable or human-judgment terms; if they are not machine-testable, the queue can still behave as an infinite-loop generator framed as 'discuss with Prism until no concerns'.
missing_evidence: A real complete-revival-e2e outer-run receipt showing that attach_e2e_run_retention_result executed, produced redcap-e2e-run-retention-after-run.json, and deleted stale-active directories without any manual prune command.
The concrete exit_criteria text from assets/contracts/open-loop-closure-queue.json and a machine-checkable condition that terminates the queue automatically.

A diff or inventory of exactly which private-content markers were removed from assets/docs/cap-revival-manual.md, plus confirmation that no path/semantic references to ~/.cap/identity.md remain in the public document.
minimum_fix: Execute one full complete-revival-e2e run with stale-active cleanup enabled, capture the generated redcap-e2e-run-retention-after-run.json as the primary evidence, and verify no manual prune was needed. Then expose the queue's exit_criteria and make at least one termination condition automatically testable. For the manual, publish a redacted diff or marker list so the boundary fix is inspectable.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The previous Prism concern explicitly warned that manual prune/dry-run and self-check with skipped probes do not constitute completion. The current submission repeats exactly that pattern while claiming integration. This is the loop signal: the main AI may be substituting 'the code supports it' for 'it ran and worked'.

user_intent_alignment: Partial. The user asked to integrate E2E cache governance into the per-round process, not to add the capability; the user asked for a task queue with exit conditions, not just a JSON field; the user asked for a path-independent manual that respects the public/private boundary, not one that merely passes a scan. The claims are modest, but the evidence underneath them is still one layer short of satisfying the original intent.
